Dear Customer,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Lori from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

I apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused, but do not worry, we will do our best to help you.

Checked with our engineer, please help us do some tests to find out the problem, so that we can provide corresponding help.

1. Please measure the voltage of the +BAT- terminals (11# and 12#) on the control board to see whether it is above 22VDC. If the voltage is below 22VDC, please check whether the output voltage of the adapter is 36VDC. If so, disconnect the batteries from the control board and measure the output voltage of the batteries to see whether it is above 22VDC. If the voltage of the batteries is also below 22VDC, please keep the batteries charged fully to try it again. If it still cannot work, please check the batteries. Kindly note that a 24V 12Ah battery (or 2pcs 12V batteries connected in series may function as 24V) is required to power the gate opener. Marine or Automotive type battery is compatible.

2. Disconnect all accessories from the control board first (just leave the power source and the arm). And disable the photocell function by turning the dip switch #3 off. Then erase all remotes codes from the control board and reprogram them to have a try. If it fails, please instantaneously short (plug the wire in, then pull it out immediately) the push button terminals (4# and 5#) to check whether the opener can work.

How to instantaneously short the “O/S/C COM” terminals:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VdDhyHZxmpQE5pG7BYHOJi5GYb7iZHFS/view?usp=sharing

3. If there is still no luck, please release the clutches on the arm and push the gate to the middle position firstly. And engage the clutches and press the remote to see whether the gate can run towards the both directions. If it still doesn’t help, please

4. Please check the motor. Connect the red & black wires of the arm to the DC 24V power source directly, the motor should run, and then exchange the polarity of the wires, the motor should run in the opposite direction. If the motor runs in both directions, the motor itself is good. Please connect the black & red wires back to the control board and continue.

5. Disconnect the BLUE, GREEN & YELLOW wires of the faulty arm from the control board, use two jumper wires to short the ULT, COM & DLT terminals to which the wires were connected, and then press the remote to see if the opener can run.

Please let me know the result one by one.

Videos showing the problem and pictures of the whole control board are much appreciated for further judgement. You can directly send the video to my E-mail via the attachment. Thank you again for being a valued customer! Your complete satisfaction is what we strive for. We at TOPENS are always standing by and ready to help.

Dear Customer,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Heidi from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

I apologize for any inconvenience this issue may have caused, but do not worry, we will do our best to help you. All TOPENS products are backed by a 12-month warranty.

Checked with our engineer, please help us do some tests to find out the problem, so that we can provide corresponding help.

Since you mentioned the lock still unlocks but the motor won't function, please first confirm whether you hear the motor running but the arm does not move, or if the motor is completely silent. Based on what you described, the initial steps below assume the motor activates but the arm fails to move.

1. Disengage the clutch and manually push the moving-rod to the middle position. Then, press the remote control to test for movement.

2. If the arm still does not move, re-engage the clutch and detach the arm from the gate. While pushing the moving-rod inward, rotate the front mount clockwise. If the arm begins to move, the screw nut may have disengaged from the screw rod at the far end. Once the arm is back in the middle position, use the remote control to test operation again.

3. Once the arm functions properly, use a screwdriver to loosen the screw on Limit Switch B. Slide the switch slightly inward and re-tighten the screw to prevent future over-extension. For additional guidance, please refer to this help article: https://topens.com/blogs/blog-posts/how-to-retract-the-moving-rod-when-the-opener-arm-extends-too-much

4. If the opener arm is partially extended or fully retracted and the moving-rod does not move despite motor activation, ensure that the clutch is fully and correctly engaged. If engagement appears normal, disassemble the opener arm and check whether clutch components (Part B and Part C) are properly aligned. If not, manually rotate the front mount until proper alignment is achieved.

5. Verify the connection between the screw rod and the clutch component with bearing (Part C). Also inspect the moving-rod’s screw nut for signs of damage or excessive wear.

6. If all visible components appear intact and operational, but abnormal or excessive noise is present in the motor area, the issue may lie within the motor’s reduction gearbox. Internal gear damage or slippage can prevent the arm from moving, even if the motor is running. In this case, please dismantle the gearbox of the motor and check the gears inside.

Please let me know the result one by one. Kindly also share some videos showing the control board and the arm when you attempt to operate it. If the attachments are too large, you can share the video link through Dropbox, iCloud, or Google Drive. If you have not already, please reply with your order number and your shipping address including zip code and phone number so we can assist you further if a replacement is needed.

Thank you again for being a valued customer! Your complete satisfaction is what we strive for. We at TOPENS are always standing by and ready to help.

Best regards,
Heidi
TOPENS Customer Service Team

Dear Nick,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Heidi from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

I understand you are looking to purchase two dual swing opener kits for your two sets of gates and need clarification on the differences between several models. Do not worry, I am happy to help you select the best option.

All TOPENS products are backed by a 12-month warranty, and we provide lifetime technical support.

Our Recommendation: The AT1202, AT602, A8132, and KD902 are all dual swing gate openers, but they vary in power and features. Since your gates are lightweight aluminum (20-30kg each) and 3m long, the AT602 would be a suitable and cost-effective choice. The A8132 or AT1202 offer more powerful motors, which provides extra margin, especially useful on windy days or if the gates ever become slightly harder to move over time. The KD902 is a high-duty cycle hydraulic model, which is typically overkill for a residential setup like yours.

Regarding your questions about remote control:
The M12 remote has four buttons, and each can be programmed independently. You can program one button to open only your gate, another button to open only the neighbor's gate, and a third button to open both gates simultaneously. This way, you and the new owners can have remotes tailored to your specific access needs. For your requirement, you would program the desired buttons on your 6 remotes and their 2 remotes accordingly.

The TC196 WiFi remote works through the TOPENS eLink app. Within the app, you can create and name separate controllers for each gate opener, so you can choose to open one gate or both from your smartphone.

Your plan to wire in TC175P touch panels and TC148 switches is perfectly suitable for this installation.
